H2CA37304.name: Sydney Kamlager-Dove
H2CA37304.bio: Representative for California's 37th Congressional District; former California State Senator and Assemblywoman.

positions.stance: Focused on "expanding voting rights."
Focused on "reproductive justice."
Focused on "health care for all."
Supports "criminal justice reform focused on diversion, redemption, and rehabilitation."
Supports "job creation to create economic justice and opportunities for all communities."

H6CA37339.name: Samantha Mota
H6CA37339.bio: Activist, advocate and organizer; appointed in 2021 to Santa Monica's Public Safety Reform & Oversight Commission.

positions.stance: Will support the Raise the Wage Act, expand the Earned Income Tax Credit, and raise corporate tax rates.
Wants a national paid family leave policy for mothers and fathers and a $5,000 expansion of the Child Tax Credit.
Will advocate legislation prohibiting warrantless surveillance of citizens, repealing FISA, and rescinding the Authorization for Use of Military Force.
Will advocate "direct federal funding for community-based projects, initiatives, and programs to enhance community development and resilience."
Will fight for Medicare for All, including dental, vision, preventive and mental care, and drug price negotiation.

H4CA31212.name: Pedro Casas
H4CA31212.bio: Retired U.S. Army colonel and clinical, forensic and aero-medical psychologist.

positions.stance: Pledges to "provide proactive leadership to address the specific needs of the 38th Congressional District."
Wants to "enhance educational opportunities for local children to access top-tier universities."
Pledges to "combat the deadly impact of fentanyl on our youth."
Wants to "enhance public safety to prevent criminals from being incentivized to commit further offenses."
Supports "restricting biological men from competing against women" in sports.

H6CA38139.name: Hilda Solis
H6CA38139.bio: Los Angeles County Supervisor and Chair of the Metro Board of Directors; former U.S. Secretary of Labor under President Obama.

positions.stance: Says working people are "under assault by the Trump Administration" and she will fight for workers, immigrants, reproductive rights, the Affordable Care Act and democracy.
Has "always prioritized fighting for clean air, water, and open green space."
Supports ensuring all people, "regardless of their zip code, have access to quality health care, medical facilities, and the resources needed to thrive."
"Committed towards creating and preserving affordable housing for all residents in innovative and sustainable ways."
Believes "we need to shift the focus from punishment and incarceration to support and resources" in the justice system.

H2CA43245.name: Mark Takano
H2CA43245.bio: Member of Congress representing California's 39th District; former high school teacher and Riverside Community College District trustee.

H6CA39145.name: Steve Manos
H6CA39145.bio: Business owner since 1996, Lake Elsinore City Council member since 2012 and mayor in 2015, 2019, 2024 and 2026; past president of the Inland Valleys Association of Realtors.

positions.stance: Will seek policies that "protect this nation from all threats - both foreign and domestic."
Will seek policies that "ensure parental rights are never threatened."
Wants to "remove the regulatory barriers that increase the cost of housing and basic needs" and calls affordable, market-rate housing the greatest need.
"We must immediately fund freeway repairs along the 215 freeway, along with increased transportation capacity for our growing region."
"Our Veterans need our continued support."

H2CA37023.name: Ken Calvert
H2CA37023.bio: U.S. Representative and Chairman of the House Defense Appropriations Subcommittee; former small business owner in the restaurant and commercial brokerage and development industries.

H8CA39240.name: Young Kim
H8CA39240.bio: Member of Congress; former California State Assemblymember.

positions.stance: Working "to lower the cost of gas, groceries, and utilities and make it easier for families to get ahead."
Has fought "to lower healthcare and prescription drug costs for seniors and protect Medicare."
Says accountability "starts with protecting taxpayer dollars from waste, fraud, and abuse."
"I support term limits because public service should be about serving the American people, not personal or financial gain."
Introduced legislation to ban members of Congress from trading individual stocks while in office.
Working "to lower costs for Southern California's families," from housing to groceries.
Fighting to restore Medicaid funding, protect ACA subsidies, lower prescription drug costs, and protect coverage for pre-existing conditions.
Believes "no one is above the law, including elected officials"; supports banning members of Congress and their families from trading stocks.
Has fought "to protect families from intimidation and inhumane treatment" by ICE and championed efforts to block ICE funding.

H2CA47188.name: Robert Garcia
H2CA47188.bio: Member of Congress; former Mayor of Long Beach.

positions.stance: Calls defending democracy "the most important issue facing Congress today"; strongly supported Prop 50.
"I strongly support the Green New Deal"; leading the Green New Deal on Transportation to electrify public transit fleets.
Fights for a nationwide $15 minimum wage, overtime reform, public banks, expanded paid family leave, and the earned income tax credit.
Fights "for universal child care and pre-k in Congress."
Fighting "to expand pathways to citizenship for undocumented residents" and end legal discrimination against them.

H0CA48172.name: Brian Burley
H0CA48172.bio: Trustee on the Huntington Beach City School District Board with a career in information technology and higher education.

positions.stance: Will "advocate for tax relief to families and business owners."
Will "take a stand against illegal immigration."
Will "fully support our law enforcement and our military."
Will "fight to restore American family values."

H6CA43188.name: Cristian Morales
H6CA43188.bio: Businessman with a 20-plus-year career in manufacturing, including automotive, aerospace and defense.

positions.stance: Wants to cut taxes and regulations, lower energy, gasoline, food and housing costs, and "make government live within its means."
Supports banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks and enforcing anti-corruption laws regardless of party.
Wants to increase housing supply by reducing permitting and regulatory barriers and expand opportunities for first-time homebuyers.
Will "defend the constitutional rights of law-abiding gun owners" and crack down on violent criminals and illegal firearms trafficking.
Supports more healthcare choices and competition, price transparency, lower drug prices, and protecting patients with pre-existing conditions.

H6CA44103.name: Nanette Barragán
H6CA44103.bio: Congresswoman representing California's 44th District since 2017; former councilmember and business advisor.

positions.stance: Says Medicare and Social Security should be strengthened and expanded, reducing fraud and waste and ensuring everyone pays their fair share.
Wants early childhood education funded and available to all and college made more affordable, with free-to-low-cost education in the future.
Supports comprehensive immigration reform, "a path to citizenship for immigrants," and the DREAM Act.
"She will fight to combat climate change and work to transition us to clean, renewable energy," ending subsidies for polluters.
Supports job training, small businesses, clean energy investment, a higher minimum wage, and equal pay for women.

H6CA44210.name: Genevieve Angel
H6CA44210.bio: Family nurse practitioner, senior healthcare executive and small-business owner.

positions.stance: Focused on lowering the cost of living, supporting working families, and expanding economic opportunity.
Focused on strengthening community safety, supporting "accountability and effective enforcement," and addressing rising crime trends.
Focused on lowering out-of-pocket costs, expanding access to care, and improving system efficiency.
Focused on "secure borders," "fair legal pathways," and "policies that work in the real world."

H4CA45170.name: Derek Tran
H4CA45170.bio: Army veteran, workers' rights attorney, pharmacy owner, and Representative for California's 45th Congressional District.

positions.stance: Is "100% pro-choice" and supports funding for Planned Parenthood and access to birth control and cancer screenings.
Supports raising teacher wages, investing in public schools, early childhood education, and more vocational education and job training.
"Derek believes healthcare should be a right, not a privilege"; opposes Medicaid cuts and will defend Medicare.
Will fight cuts to Social Security and Medicare and work to strengthen voting rights and "defend our free and fair elections."
Supports limiting the influence of lobbyists and special interests and "strong campaign finance reforms and more transparency."

H6CA45191.name: Chuong Vo
H6CA45191.bio: Former Mayor of Cerritos and 28-year law-enforcement officer.

positions.stance: Will back law enforcement, push for body-worn cameras and de-escalation training, and increase penalties for fentanyl trafficking.
Will vote to cut wasteful spending that fuels inflation and "protect Social Security and Medicare for today's seniors."
Wants homelessness funding tied to accountability and outcomes, prioritizing mental-health and addiction treatment, and enforcing no-camping rules near schools and parks.
Supports expanding CTE and STEM programs, evidence-based reading instruction, and ensuring "parents have a real voice" in education.
Supports "secure borders and faster asylum decisions" and modernizing legal immigration.

H6CA46116.name: Lou Correa
H6CA46116.bio: Member of Congress for California's 46th District; former California State Assemblymember, State Senator, Orange County Supervisor, banker, attorney and real estate broker.

positions.stance: "I support charter schools and school vouchers to allow all parents to choose the best education for their children."
"To make our streets safe again, we need to recruit more police and enforce our laws."
"We need to secure our border so that we can develop a consistent immigration policy."
"Reducing taxes and regulations on small businesses will create jobs and renew our communities."
Says the debt cannot be solved without reforming welfare and entitlement programs; his plan would save "over $1 trillion per year."

H4CA47085.name: Dave Min
H4CA47085.bio: Member of Congress for California's 47th District; former California State Senator, UC Irvine law professor and SEC enforcement attorney.

positions.stance: Says democracy and the rule of law face attack from the Trump administration and "we must treat this crisis of democracy with the urgency it deserves."
Supports an all-of-the-above approach that reduces barriers to building housing while funding and subsidizing affordable housing.
Voted against Medicaid and Medicare funding cuts and to protect the premium tax credits Californians rely on.
"Women should have full autonomy over their own bodies and their ability to make their own healthcare decisions."
Supports expanding background checks and red flag laws and renewing the assault weapons ban.

H6CA47114.name: Jenny Le Roux
H6CA47114.bio: Executive Director of CAL DOGE and business owner who co-built companies in energy and financial services.

positions.stance: Will work to rein in federal spending, push permitting reform for housing construction, and reduce the tax burden on small businesses.
Supports fully funding border security, ending catch-and-release, closing asylum loopholes, and opposes federal funding for sanctuary cities.
Will demand mandatory public spending reports for major federal programs and independent, real-time audits of high-risk programs.
Will demand full transparency in admissions at federally funded universities and support enforcing the Civil Rights Act against race-based decisions.
Will push for "outcome-based requirements attached to every federal homelessness grant."

H6CA49128.name: Jim Desmond
H6CA49128.bio: San Diego County Supervisor, former Mayor of San Marcos, U.S. Navy veteran and Delta Air Lines pilot for 33 years.

positions.stance: Will work toward "lowering taxes, reducing overregulation, and curbing out-of-control costs" driving seniors and families out of the state.
Supports funding "treatment-first programs that address the root causes of homelessness: addiction and mental illness," with federal dollars tied to results.
Will fight to protect borders from illegal crossings, create an efficient legal immigration process, and stop people "skipping the line."
Opposes mandating costly energy alternatives and supports letting families choose energy sources "from natural gas to renewables."
Proposes offering free vocational education and training to encourage volunteer military service.

H6CA48310.name: Marni von Wilpert
H6CA48310.bio: Workers' rights attorney in the Obama Administration, former prosecutor and San Diego Deputy City Attorney, and City Council member.

positions.stance: Will work "to get ICE's masked mobs off our streets"; supports secure borders and legal pathways to citizenship for long-term residents and Dreamers.
Supports banning members of Congress from trading stocks, passing the John Lewis Voting Rights Act, and overturning Citizens United.
Will protect and expand the ACA with a public option, oppose Social Security cuts or privatization, and expand Medicare drug price negotiation.
Will fight "Trump's tariff war" and corporations raising prices, and crack down on wage theft.
Will cut red tape to build more affordable housing and pass the PRO Act to strengthen workers' rights to organize.

H8CA49058.name: Mike Levin
H8CA49058.bio: Member of Congress for California's 49th District since 2019; former attorney focused on environmental and energy regulatory compliance.

positions.stance: Leads the Energy Bills Relief Act to lower electricity bills and helped write a bill to stop fuel price gouging.
Supports legislation to combat climate change and secured federal funding for drought resistance and water infrastructure to lower wildfire risk.
Supports the Stop Price Gouging in Grocery Stores Act; says Trump's tariffs are "driving up families' bills and destroying small businesses."
Supported the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and the CHIPS and Science Act to create jobs and bring microchip production back to America.
"Mike has never supported defunding the police, and he never will"; supports increased police funding and cosponsors the Invest to Protect Act.

H6CA49169.name: Armen Kurdian
H6CA49169.bio: Retired U.S. Navy captain with 25 years of service.

positions.stance: Will fight to lower the cost of living, "cut wasteful federal spending, oppose tax increases," and support small businesses.
Supports "an all-of-the-above energy strategy" to lower energy costs and achieve American energy independence.
Will fight to bring back manufacturing, expand apprenticeships and trade education, and cut regulations pushing employers out of California.
Will back police and first responders and "crack down on fentanyl and cartel trafficking."
Will fight for veterans' healthcare and benefits and "fully fund our national defense."

H2CA52089.name: Scott Peters
H2CA52089.bio: Member of Congress for California's 50th District; former San Diego City Council President and Chair of the Port.

positions.stance: Wants to "build more homes, get more people off the street and into housing, and cut the red tape that slows both down."
Wants to "bring lower drug prices to more families, keep premiums in check," and make mental health and addiction care easier to get.
Wants to finish the South Bay treatment plant and keep federal money coming to stop sewage and reopen beaches.
Wants to "speed up clean energy projects, prevent the next big wildfire, and plan now for higher seas around San Diego Bay."
Has fought to steer Navy repair work to local shipyards and says "keeping promises to people who served" is the floor.

H6CA50324.name: Steve Cohen
H6CA50324.bio: Broadcast journalist for fifty years and former KUSI-TV News Director for twenty years.

positions.stance: Will fight for "expanding housing supply, cracking down on corporate price manipulation," and economic policy that works for residents.
Will work to lower prescription drug costs, protect coverage for pre-existing conditions, and hold insurance companies accountable.
Will "defend Social Security and Medicare from cuts."
Will demand transparency in government spending and oppose wasteful earmarks.

H8CA49074.name: Sara Jacobs
H8CA49074.bio: Congresswoman for California's 51st District since 2021; former U.S. State Department, UNICEF and United Nations policy staffer and founding CEO of Project Connect.
